learn.hook: 12 + 8 and 5 × 4 look totally different, but they are secret twins — both are worth 20!
points: An arithmetic expression is numbers joined by +, −, × or ÷, like 4 × 25 + 10.
The value of an expression is the number you get when you work it out.
Different expressions can have the same value: 12 + 8 = 5 × 4 = 20.
We compare expressions using =, < or > by comparing their values.
A word problem can be written as an expression first, then calculated.

example.q: Kabir buys 3 samosas at ₹15 each and one juice for ₹20. Write an expression for the total and find its value.

learn.reallife: Every shopping bill is an arithmetic expression: quantity × price for each item, all added up.

games.title: Match each expression to its value

quiz.explain: Multiply first: 6 × 8 = 48. Then 48 − 10 = 38.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 8 − 10 first
Works left to right and forgets to multiply first

quiz.q: Aisha has ₹100. She buys 4 pens at ₹12 each. Which expression shows the money left?
quiz.explain: The pens cost 4 × 12. We take that away from 100: 100 − 4 × 12.
quiz.mistake: Writes the numbers in the order they appear instead of what is happening

quiz.q: Aisha had ₹100 and spent 4 × ₹12 on pens. How much money is left?
quiz.explain: 4 × 12 = 48 was spent. 100 − 48 = 52 is left.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the price of only one pen

quiz.q: Which sign goes in the box? 25 × 4 ☐ 98 + 3
quiz.explain: 25 × 4 = 100 and 98 + 3 = 101. 100 is less than 101, so we use <.
quiz.mistake: Guesses that the multiplication side must be bigger

quiz.q: A Diwali rangoli has 5 rows of 7 diyas, plus 3 extra diyas in the centre. How many diyas are there in all?
quiz.explain: 5 rows of 7 is 5 × 7 = 35. Add the 3 in the centre: 35 + 3 = 38.
quiz.mistake: Adds 7 + 3 first and then multiplies by 5

options: 2 notebooks at ₹30 each and 3 erasers at ₹10 each
30 notebooks shared by 2 children and 10 erasers
quiz.explain: 2 × 30 is the cost of 2 notebooks at ₹30. 3 × 10 is the cost of 3 erasers at ₹10. The + joins the two costs.
quiz.mistake: Reads × as sharing (division)

quiz.explain: Divide first: 48 ÷ 6 = 8. Then 8 + 2 = 10.
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 + 2 first, then divides 48 by 8

teach.ask: Gappu sees '3 × 15 + 20' on a canteen bill. What is an expression, and how do you find its value?
teach.praise: Yay! Gappu found the bill total all by himself: ₹65!
teach.nudge: What do we get when we work out an expression?

learn.hook: Is 2 + 3 × 4 equal to 20 or 14? Without a rule, friends would fight! The order rule ends the fight.
points: Next do × and ÷, going from left to right.
Last do + and −, going from left to right.
Terms are the parts of an expression joined by + or −. In 20 + 3 × 5 − 8 the terms are 20, 3 × 5 and 8.
learn.reallife: Calculators and computer programs all follow this same order, so everyone in the world gets the same answer.

quiz.explain: Multiply before adding: 3 × 4 = 12, then 2 + 12 = 14.
quiz.mistake: Works strictly left to right: 2 + 3 = 5, then 5 × 4

quiz.explain: Divide first: 10 ÷ 5 = 2. Then 30 − 2 = 28.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts first: 30 − 10 = 20, then 20 ÷ 5

quiz.explain: Brackets first: 8 + 4 = 12. Then 12 × 3 = 36.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the brackets and multiplies 4 × 3 first

quiz.explain: Multiply first: 4 × 6 = 24. Then left to right: 50 − 24 = 26, and 26 + 3 = 29.
quiz.mistake: Adds 24 + 3 first and subtracts 27, or forgets the last term

quiz.explain: × and ÷ are done left to right. 36 ÷ 6 = 6, then 6 × 2 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Thinks × must always come before ÷, so does 6 × 2 first

quiz.explain: Terms are separated by + and −. The terms are 7, 2 × 5 and 9. That makes 3 terms.
quiz.mistake: Counts every number as a separate term

quiz.q: Harpreet buys 3 kg of apples at ₹80 per kg and 2 kg of bananas at ₹40 per kg. Which expression gives the total cost?
quiz.explain: Apples cost 3 × 80 and bananas cost 2 × 40. Add the two costs: 3 × 80 + 2 × 40 = 240 + 80 = ₹320.
quiz.mistake: Adds all the kilograms and all the prices together

quiz.explain: Inside the bracket, multiply first: 5 × 4 = 20, so the bracket is 20 + 20 = 40. Then 100 − 40 = 60.
quiz.mistake: Inside the bracket, adds 20 + 5 first and gets 25 × 4 = 100

teach.ask: Gappu got 20 for 2 + 3 × 4 and his friend got 14. Who is right, and what is the rule?
teach.praise: Wonderful! Now Gappu knows why the answer is 14!
teach.nudge: Which operation do we do before adding?

learn.hook: A minus sign standing outside a bracket is like a mirror — every sign inside flips when you open it!
points: If a − sign is before a bracket, change the sign of every term inside when you remove it: 50 − (20 + 5) = 50 − 20 − 5.
Also 50 − (20 − 5) = 50 − 20 + 5, because taking away less leaves more.
If a + sign is before a bracket, just remove it: 30 + (8 − 3) = 30 + 8 − 3.
Terms being added can be swapped and grouped in any way: 27 + 46 + 73 = (27 + 73) + 46.
A number times a bracket can be split: 6 × (10 + 3) = 6 × 10 + 6 × 3.

example.q: Meena had ₹200. She spent ₹45 on a book and ₹35 on colours. How much is left?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers use smart grouping to add bills in their heads, like pairing ₹65 and ₹35 to make ₹100.

games.title: Bracket truth test
items: Both sides equal 15. The minus flips the + inside.
Swapping does not work for subtraction: 15 is not the same as −15.
Added terms can be swapped. Both equal 127.

quiz.explain: Taking away (20 + 5) means taking away 20 and also taking away 5: 50 − 20 − 5 = 25.
quiz.mistake: Removes the bracket without changing the sign inside

quiz.explain: The bracket is 30 − 10 = 20, and 80 − 20 = 60. Opened up, it is 80 − 30 + 10 = 60.
quiz.mistake: Opens the bracket as 80 − 30 − 10 without flipping the sign
Subtracts just 2 instead of 7 × 2

quiz.explain: 36 + 64 = 100 is a friendly pair. Then 100 + 58 = 158.
quiz.mistake: Makes a carrying slip when adding in the given order
Multiplies only the first part, then adds 5

quiz.q: Joseph had 45 marbles. He gave 12 to Riya and 8 to Arjun. Which expression does NOT give the marbles left?
quiz.explain: He gave away 12 + 8 = 20, so 25 are left. 45 − (12 − 8) = 41, which is wrong. The other three all give 25.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any bracket arrangement gives the same value
Opens the bracket but does not flip every sign inside

quiz.q: Which one has the same value as 40 − 15 + 5?
quiz.explain: 40 − 15 + 5 = 30. Moving whole terms with their own signs keeps the value: 40 + 5 − 15 = 30 too.
quiz.mistake: Moves the numbers but leaves the signs behind

teach.ask: Gappu wrote 50 − (20 + 5) = 50 − 20 + 5. Was he right? How do you open a bracket with a minus in front?
teach.praise: Brilliant! Gappu now opens brackets like a pro!
teach.nudge: What happens to the signs inside when there is a minus outside?
